amanda: Heads up — noticed a p99 jump in production at ~21:40 UTC across a subset of routes. Correlates with heavier long-prompt traffic + a spike in KV evictions after the kernel swap in last deploy.

perf-bot: perf report attached: p95 baseline +12ms, p99 +180ms on routes: /generate-chat (models: redwood-alpha-v2, redwood-beta-quant). KV eviction rate x3. Stack sampling shows more time in kernel_recompile path. https://perf.internal/reds/2077 (ci summary) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: Can reproduce locally with a script that replays the long prompt harness + tool-call stubs. Repro steps: `scripts/repro/replay_long_tool_loop.sh --seed=42 --rate=100`

sam: Quick profiling snippet (top 3):
```
# top by cpu (samples)
1. kernel_recompile (42%)
2. kv_cache_miss/rehydrate (21%)
3. scheduler:microbatch_wait (12%)

# callsite stack example
serve_loop -> kernel_dispatch -> maybe_recompile -> aten::compile_kernel
```

jen: Interesting — two potential amplification factors: long prompt seqlen causing kernel selection to pick a 'wide' kernel (higher scratch mem) and tool-call loops repeatedly invalidating and warming KV entries. Together they push microbatches to the slow path.

kai: Confirmed: when a request includes nested tool-call with callback and regen we see KV keys churn: tool_call_id + session_context variants => many small unique prefixes so prefix cache hit plummets.

amanda: Example log excerpt from prod trace: `req=8a2f tool_call=start callback=invoke_tool() -> gen -> callback_regen` repeated 3x with slightly different context tokens each time. Latency profile: first call 48ms, second 210ms (kernel recompile), third 430ms (kv rehydrate + microbatch stall).

sam: My hypothesis: the new kernel chooser uses a heuristic that favors a single fused kernel for long sequences; that kernel has a slower compile path when called with new token shapes, and it triggers a fallback path that serializes subsequent microbatches. Also KV eviction makes rehydrate expensive.

jen: Options to mitigate quickly: 1) pin kernel choice for redwood-beta-quant to previous kernel (v2.7-stable) for latency-SLO routes; 2) reduce microbatch target for routes with tool-calls to 1 or 2; 3) temporarily extend KV TTL/pin prefixes to prevent churn for in-flight sessions.

kai: I'd add: enable hedging for request ages > 150ms (issue speculative second replica) to avoid long tails from recompile path. Also we can add a fast-path kernel that avoids JIT on first use (warmup-only mode).

amanda: Quick config I want to try in a canary (route override):
```json
{
  "route": "/generate-chat",
  "model": "redwood-beta-quant",
  "overrides": {
    "kernel": "v2.7-stable",
    "microbatch_target": 1,
    "kv_prefix_pin": ["session", "tool_call_id"],
    "hedging_ms": 150
  }
}
```

sam: Running canary now against a 100qps replay with long prompts + simulated tool-calls. I'll post perf guardrail numbers in 10m.

perf-bot: Canary started at 21:51 UTC on pool: canary-3 (tag: kernel-pin-2077). Baseline vs canary (partial): p99 reduced from +180ms -> +45ms after kernel pin + microbatch=1. KV hit-rate for pinned prefixes improved from 62% -> 89%.

jen: Nice. If that holds we should roll patch to the SLO routes and schedule a longer-term fix: (a) refine kernel chooser heuristics to consider JIT warm cost and batch occupancy, (b) add KV prefix coalescing for tool-call patterns, (c) better locality-aware batching so microbatches don't serialize behind recompile.

kai: I'll open two PRs: one to expose kernel override per-route and one to add a fast-path kernel compile cache keyed by (model, seq_len_bucket, dtype).

amanda: Thanks everyone. Action items: sam keep canary running for 30m then push to 10% if stable; kai PRs + tests; jen follow-up bug for KV prefix heuristics; I'll draft incident note if we decide to maintain kernel pin >24h. :thumbsup:

sam: Canary steady for 12m, p99 stable at +50ms. No new error budget burn yet. Will escalate to 10% at 22:10 UTC.

kai: PRs opened: #4123 (route kernel override), #4124 (compile-cache). Linking here.

amanda: Good progress. Also want an offline postmortem root-cause draft that separates: (1) kernel selection JIT/warm cost under long-seq degenerate cases, (2) KV prefix churn due to tool-call variant contexts, (3) microbatch serialization policy interaction. Will assign owners after canary completes.

perf-bot: Perf alert auto-closed after canary improvement. Logged as incident-207777 in tracker.

jen: One more note — add synthetic eval that simulates nested tool-call + regen to our regression suite so this doesn't regress silently.

amanda: Agreed. Thanks team.
